samples.summary: The eval subsystem's canonical doc is not updated for the new reviewer identity or the new store layout
samples.evidence:
`scripts/agent/eval/README.md` is the index/design doc for this directory (there is no `docs/design/*` doc for the eval harness — grep for `by-config|panel_sha|panel_digest|scripts/agent/eval` under `docs/design/` returns nothing). The diff changes a data model and a stored path layout but leaves the doc stating the superseded facts:

- L291-298 §"Which reviewer ran": "Every envelope carries `panel_sha`, and it is not optional … the pair `(config_hash, panel_sha)` is what 'same reviewer' means." After this change the envelope also requires `panel_digest` (`store.mjs` `validateRunEnvelope`), and the digest — not the sha — is what a cross-run score is keyed by.
- L19 module table: "`config-hash.mjs` … the reviewer is the pair `(config_hash, panelSha)`", and the table has no row for the new `panel-identity.mjs`, `run.mjs`'s new `--panel-digest` flag, or the new operator CLI.
- L435-446 "The layout under a root" documents the store layout; the cross-run score directory moved from `<config-hash>__<corpus>` to `<config-hash>__<panel-digest>__<corpus>` and legacy directories are now silently unreadable, which is exactly the kind of fact this section exists to record.

CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16 and :58-60 require the doc to be written/updated in the same change as the code. `pnpm verify:doc-index` only demands *top-level* `scripts/` entries (scripts/README.md:24), so nothing mechanical will catch this.
searchedFor: Read scripts/agent/eval/README.md (module table, §Which reviewer ran, layout section)
Grep verify:doc-index across repo; read scripts/README.md:24

samples.summary: score-all always hands the digest down as `--panel-digest`, so envelope-read digests are recorded as `reconstructed` — the primary lane mislabels its own attribution
samples.evidence:
`scoreAll` resolves the panel from the store (`score-all.mjs:724`: `panelDigestArg ?? resolvePanelDigest({records: store.panelDigestRecords(ids)}).digest`) and then `panelFlags` (`:622`) pushes `--panel-digest <digest>` for every real digest, regardless of where it came from. In the child, `report.mjs`'s `resolvePanel` treats any `--panel-digest` as an assertion — it returns `source: "reconstructed"` and prints `panel_digest ... was STATED on the command line, not read from the runs` — and `withPanelStamp` writes that into the payload, which `validateScorePanel` then accepts.

So once runs actually record digests, every cross-run score filed through the normal `score-all` lane will claim `panel_digest_source: "reconstructed"` ("stated rather than observed") for a digest that was in fact READ off the envelopes, and the `envelopes` value becomes reachable only by invoking `report.mjs --persist` by hand. That inverts the point of correction 4 in the task doc (`docs/tasks/active/20260820-eval-panel-digest-todo.md:125-134`): the closed vocabulary exists so "no field claims an observation nobody made", and here the honest, stronger attribution is thrown away by the wiring. The score-all test fixture bakes the same rule in (`score-all.test.mjs:697`: `const source = stated ? "reconstructed" : resolved?.source;`), so nothing reddens. A `--panel-digest-source` hand-down, or distinguishing "driver read it" from "operator stated it", would keep the vocabulary meaningful.

samples.summary: `comparisonIdFor`'s docblock was orphaned onto `withPanelStamp`, leaving the comparison-id rule documenting the wrong function
samples.evidence: report.mjs:316-333 is the docblock about the comparison id ("The comparison's identity, DERIVED from the comparability key…", plus the new ⚠ note about the report filename changing). It is now immediately followed by a second docblock (:334-347) and `export function withPanelStamp` (:348). `comparisonIdFor` at :355 has no docblock at all. In a module whose docblocks are the primary design record, the reasoning for the report filename now sits above an unrelated function and the function it describes is undocumented.

samples.summary: `listRuns({ panelDigest })` is an unrequested filter with no caller
samples.evidence: `listRuns` gains a `panelDigest` filter (`store.mjs:1105`, `:1119`). Grepping `listRuns(` across `scripts/` finds only `store.test.mjs:783-810`, which exercises `configHash`, `corpusVersion` and `panelSha` and never the new parameter, and no production call site anywhere. The task doc's change list (docs/tasks/active/20260820-eval-panel-digest-todo.md:64-73) names `_scorePath`, `putScore`, `getScore`, `comparisonIdFor`/`buildReport` and `writtenPaths` — not `listRuns`. Speculative surface added ahead of a need.

samples.summary: The scoring lane's workflow is not extended for the new key, so the documented migration and the mixed-panel opt-out are unreachable from CI
samples.evidence: `eval-score.yml` invokes `score-all.mjs` (:199-205) with only `--root/--corpus-version/--config-hash/--runs/--out/--emit-dir`, and its `workflow_dispatch` inputs (:55-75) offer no `panel_digest` or `allow_mixed_panel`. The task doc's migration decision (docs/tasks/active/20260820-eval-panel-digest-todo.md:260-263) recommends re-scoring via `score-all.mjs … --panel-digest sha256:cbfa31bb…`, which this lane cannot express; and once replays record digests, a mixed pool will refuse here with no way to pass the opt-out. The `config_hash` input description (:61) also still calls it "half of the pair a score is filed under", which is no longer true.
searchedFor: Read .github/workflows/eval-score.yml inputs and the score-all invocation

samples.summary: A third private sha256 helper, duplicating `config-hash.mjs`'s exported `sha256Hex`
samples.evidence: `panel-identity.mjs` defines `const sha256 = (text) => createHash("sha256").update(text, "utf8").digest("hex")`, byte-for-byte the behaviour of the exported `config-hash.mjs:290 sha256Hex` (and of `store.mjs:264 contentSha256`). Reuse is the repo's stated default. It is arguably justified here — `config-hash.mjs:53` imports `../review-panel.mjs`, so importing it from `panel-identity.mjs` would drag the panel into `store.mjs`'s import graph — but the duplication is unexplained in a file that explains everything else, and a shared leaf helper would remove the choice.

verdict.reason: I could not find any counterexample. The eval subsystem's only prose doc, scripts/agent/eval/README.md, still states the superseded identity at :291-293 ("the pair `(config_hash, panel_sha)` is what 'same reviewer' means") and :19 ("the reviewer is the pair `(config_hash, panelSha)`"), while the code now requires `panel_digest` on every envelope (store.mjs:700) and keys cross-run scores by it (store.mjs:411 byConfigSegment(configHash, panelDigest, corpusVersion), :377 panelKeySegment). A repo-wide grep for panel_digest/panel-identity hits no markdown outside docs/tasks/active/20260820-eval-panel-digest-todo.md and the .agent-review artifacts; docs/design/ has no eval-harness doc (harness-engineering.md: 42 hits for eval/replay/corpus, zero for digest/panel_sha/byConfigSegment; docs/design/README.md: none). Two qualifications keep my confidence low rather than high: (1) the change does ship a thorough task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260820-eval-panel-digest-todo.md) recording the new module, the --panel-digest flag, the three-part key and the legacy-directory behaviour, satisfying CONTRIBUTING.md:62-65 — it just does not repair the README sentence; (2) the reviewer's third evidence bullet is wrong on the facts — README.md:435-446 lists corpus/, runs/, captures/, labels/ and no scores/ entry, so the score-path rename was never recorded there — and the module table is already non-exhaustive from earlier merged work (lines 30-32 claim complementarity/reliability/cost-latency are "not built yet" though all three modules exist), making the "no row for panel-identity.mjs" sub-point systemic pre-existing drift rather than this change's omission.

verdict.reason: The wiring is exactly as claimed. score-all.mjs:724 resolves the panel via resolvePanelDigest but keeps only `.digest`, dropping the `source` that panel-identity.mjs:464-467 deliberately sets to "envelopes" on every path ("whatever it answers was read rather than asserted"). panelFlags (score-all.mjs:622-627) then pushes `--panel-digest <digest>` for any real digest at both the persist (:597/:789) and render (:606/:801) call sites. In the child, report.mjs:3369-3377 treats any `--panel-digest` as an operator assertion — logs "was STATED on the command line, not read from the runs" and returns source "reconstructed" — which withPanelStamp (report.mjs:348-352) writes into the payload, and store.mjs:487 accepts because "reconstructed" is in PANEL_DIGEST_SOURCES. Net effect: once runs record digests, every cross-run score filed through the primary score-all lane stamps panel_digest_source "reconstructed" for a digest that was in fact read off envelopes; "envelopes" survives only when the resolution is NOT an identity (not-recorded/mixed, where no flag is handed down) or when report.mjs --persist is invoked by hand. That contradicts the stated purpose of the closed vocabulary in docs/tasks/active/20260820-eval-panel-digest-todo.md:125-134 ("no field claims an observation nobody made"), and score-all.test.mjs:695-701 encodes the same rule so no test reddens. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, nothing corrects the source before putScore, and this is a design-intent/vocabulary-semantics concern squarely in the design-fit lane. The doc's line 131 ("--panel-digest sets reconstructed in both callers") is ambiguous enough that I cannot conclude the behaviour is sanctioned rather than an oversight, and the issue's acceptance list was not available to settle it.
